props.markdown: The bench holds the 30/78 gearset of the previous screen, driven at 1,000 rpm. For each requirement, **predict** the configuration with the Willis equation first, then run the bench to check. Every run counts: aim to meet each requirement at the first run.

props.title: 3D test bench of a planetary gearset

props.instruction: Choose the held member and the member the motor drives, then run the bench. The third member is the output.

props.textAlternative:
**Text version of the test bench.** The gearset has a 30-tooth sun, three 24-tooth planets on a carrier, and a 78-tooth ring. A motor turns at 1,000 rpm. You choose which member is held by a brake and which member the motor drives; the third member is the output, and the bench measures its speed and direction.

For each requirement, write down the held member and the driven member, then check with $Z_s\,n_s + Z_r\,n_r = (Z_s + Z_r)\,n_c$.

1. Electric-drive reducer: the output must turn 3.6 times slower than the motor, in the same direction.
2. Wind-turbine speed-up: the output must turn 3.6 times faster than the motor, in the same direction.
3. Reverse gear: the output must turn the other way, 2.6 times slower than the motor.

events.description: Open the debrief table once the three requirements are met.

props.title: Six configurations, one equation
props.markdown:
| Held | Driven | Output | Ratio | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ring | Sun | Carrier | 3.6 : 1 | Strong reduction |
| Sun | Ring | Carrier | 1.38 : 1 | Mild reduction |
| Sun | Carrier | Ring | 0.72 : 1 | Mild overdrive |
| Ring | Carrier | Sun | 0.28 : 1 | Strong overdrive |
| Carrier | Sun | Ring | −2.6 : 1 | Reverse, reduction |
| Carrier | Ring | Sun | −0.38 : 1 | Reverse, overdrive |

The carrier is always the slowest member when it is not held; holding it is the only way to reverse.
